triggerReasons.message: High-risk or gate/security wording selects high-assurance intent hardening.
High-assurance work requires an independent intent-collision result.
Ambiguity, user impact, behavior change, or multi-deliverable intent makes intent collision diagnostically required.
Bug, regression, security/auth/session, benchmark, or explicit behavior-change work should have red evidence.
Broad or absolute scope wording should have scope clarification before future enforcement.

acceptanceBindings.acceptanceClaim: A pinned command configured with a validate.commands[].timeoutMs above 270s and a genuine runtime in that gap completes and yields a normal mechanical receipt via verification_evidence_add instead of being refused at 270s with [receipt_exit_nonzero]; a pinned command with no configured override still gets refused at exactly 270s as before.
acceptanceBindings.note: Single acceptance claim covering the full fix: CHK-001 red repro, CHK-002 the fix, CHK-003 regression coverage. verificationIntentRefs intentionally omitted (were originally CHK-001:happy:0/CHK-002:happy:0/CHK-003:happy:0 - a data-entry mistake, since CHK-002 happy[0] actually has custom id H-001, so CHK-002:happy:0 never resolved) after discovering the ProofStory REVIEW completeness gate requires non-waiver passing evidence for any bound intentRef, and this stories evidence-pin-immutability constraint makes several individual intentRefs permanently waiver-only even though the underlying claims are genuinely tested (see checklist.json verificationEvidence notes and findings.json F-002 through F-009).

diagnosticGaps.message: Red evidence is triggered but no current red evidence record binds baseline head/material to the correct acceptance target and green relation.

note: B-16df ProofStory contract: one acceptance binding covering the timeoutMs-config-override fix end to end, scoped at checklist level only (no per-intentRef binding) to avoid the REVIEW completeness gates non-waiver requirement on individual pinned intentRefs that this stories evidence-pin-immutability structurally cannot satisfy.
